name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
description: Hampi, in central Karnataka, India, was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire from 1336 until its sacking in 1565. By around 1500 it may have been the world's second-largest city. Its ruins now cover about 4,100 hectares beside the Tungabhadra River, with more than 1,600 remains of temples, pillared halls, forts and water structures. Worshippers still visit the Virupaksha Temple.
